comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not mark VI-002 passed before required execution**

This file's own methodology requires reconstructing every affected definition/document and verifying that VI-001 remains executable, but the completed result records no such execution; the only `Reconstruct`/`Verify` mentions are the checklist entries at lines 65-67. Marking the investigation `PASS` here gives downstream proof and conjecture artifacts a completed validation result without the evidence required by the investigation procedure.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep the VI-002 result table in sync**

This `Current Results` table still marks Property as pending, but the same file later adds Reduction Investigation 2 and summarizes Property as `Independent (Provisional)` in the final results. Readers using this earlier registry will conclude that six reductions remain unrun, which contradicts the completed summary at the end of the investigation.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep conjectures in one canonical registry**

This declares a Project-wide canonical conjecture registry even though `theory/theorems/conjectures.md` already records Project FAR conjectures, including Primitive Independence, Primitive Minimality, and Architectural Completeness. Because the charter requires a single canonical location for each canonical artifact, the new CJ-* registry creates competing IDs and statuses for the same claims.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore the research index or update its users**

Deleting this index leaves existing repository navigation and audit evidence stale: `README.md:31` and `docs/README.md:24` still point readers to `research/README.md`, and `docs/SEMANTIC_AUDIT.md:111` cites this file as evidence that research content is non-canonical until promoted. Keep the index or update those artifacts in the same change.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Create proof files before cataloging them**

This catalog now records L-001 (and the following L/P/T entries) as draft proof artifacts with canonical file paths, but I checked repo-wide with `rg --files` for these IDs and for `research/proofs/{lemmas,propositions,theorems}/`, and none of the referenced files or directories exist. Because this document is explicitly a navigation artifact and complete inventory, these new entries send readers to non-existent canonical proofs and make the proof library look normalized when the actual proof documents are absent.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Define the path used for weak connectivity**

When weak connectivity is used by the new dependency-component proof, this definition still relies on a bare `path` after direction is ignored, but the only path definition introduced above is `Directed Path`, which explicitly preserves edge direction. In any proof that depends on weak dependency components, this leaves the undirected/weak path relation undefined, so the canonical graph layer has not actually supplied the terminology P012 needs.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
Addressed by adding a canonical `Undirected Path` definition and revising weak connectivity to depend on undirected paths instead of an undefined bare path.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restrict the objective to nodes in the dependency subgraph**

For an assessment graph containing an assessment with no dependency edge, or only non-dependency edges, Definition 13 excludes that assessment from the dependency subgraph because it includes only nodes incident to dependency edges. In that context the new theorem below is scoped to assessment nodes already in the dependency subgraph, but this objective still claims every assessment belongs to a weak dependency component, reintroducing the invalid partition claim the refactor is trying to remove.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
Addressed by restricting the objective and theorem to assessment nodes in the dependency subgraph, and by adding a note that the theorem does not apply to assessment nodes outside that subgraph.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove unbacked meta-theorem coverage claims**

With this commit the only files in `frameworks/FARE/meta` are M001 and M002, but this sentence says FARE meta-theorems establish traceability, investigation soundness, and proof soundness as well; checking the new directory shows no corresponding accepted theorem documents. That makes planned or absent coverage look like an accepted result in the directory index, which can mislead audits that rely on these READMEs to describe the repository state accurately; either remove those extra properties or add/link the accepted theorem artifacts that establish them.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require completions to add missing limits**

Because this obligation only covers sequences whose required limit is already represented by the proposed completion, a candidate can omit any problematic convergent sequence and still satisfy the definition; in the extreme, an incomplete `E` can be treated as its own completion by representing no new limits. That makes completion/completeness vacuous and undermines the existing completion question in `frameworks/FARE/mathematics/conjectures/C020-evaluation-completion.md`, which asks whether every convergent sequence has a valid limit.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make cost models cover every path being measured**

This definition allows a transformation cost model to assign costs only to admissible transformations “under consideration,” but the distance definition below still takes the infimum over all admissible paths. When a path contains an admissible transformation outside that partial model, `Cost(tau)` and therefore `Cost(P)` are undefined, so `d(E_1, E_2)` is not well-defined for that evaluation space. Either require the model to cover every transformation in the path system used by distance or restrict the infimum to paths whose transformations are covered by the specified model.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Disambiguate `N(E)` for chosen neighborhood systems**

This introduces `N(E)` as the collection supplied by a particular neighborhood system, but the existing Neighborhood Family section later defines `N(E)` as every admissible neighborhood centered at `E`. In contexts where alternative neighborhood systems are admitted, this makes convergence ambiguous: it is unclear whether convergence quantifies over the selected system or over the union of every admissible neighborhood. Rename one notation or make the family explicitly relative to the chosen system.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep theorem identifiers unique**

These new index entries reuse `MT-001` through `MT-003` while the existing active proofs `frameworks/FARE/mathematics/proofs/T001-identity-path-is-geodesic.md`, `T002-path-composition-preserves-reachability.md`, and `T003-every-geodesic-is-a-path.md` still declare those same identifiers with `Accepted` status. Because the new `proofs/README.md` says the proofs directory contains active proofs and the old files were not archived or renumbered, references to `MT-001`/`MT-002`/`MT-003` now resolve to different theorem statements, making dependency citations ambiguous and corrupting the theorem index.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Consolidate project status into the existing status file**

This adds a second current-status artifact while `docs/PROJECT_STATUS.md` already states that it records the current state and should be updated when a significant milestone completes, and `docs/README.md`/`docs/ROADMAP.md` still direct readers to that existing file. With the root README now pointing at this new file, readers get two incompatible current-focus statements (`FAR Core Framework` here versus `Phase V — Methodological Foundations` in the existing status file), which violates the repo's single-canonical-location rule for status information and makes the active workstream ambiguous.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Align FARE expansion gates with the freeze policy**

This development-order rule allows FARE Mathematics to expand when FARO or FARA require it, but the same new status document's governance rules and the new milestone freeze policy restrict new FARE definitions/theorems to requirements from FAR. In a FARO- or FARA-driven request, contributors would have contradictory governance about whether mathematical expansion is permitted, so the expansion gate should match the freeze policy or explicitly explain the broader exception.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore removed canonical theory entries**

This rewrite leaves the Theory section ending after `Propositions`, but the parent map also recorded canonical locations for Lemmas, Theorems, Conjectures, Proofs, FARO-specific definitions, and Meta-Theoretic definitions; those artifacts still exist (for example `theory/proofs/proofs.md`, `theory/definitions/meta-theory-definitions.md`, and `frameworks/FARO/theory/definitions.md`). Since the map's purpose is to identify the single canonical source for major concepts, dropping these entries makes those concepts unauditable from the canonical map and violates the repository's single-canonical-location rule.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Align FARO status with existing FARO docs**

This new status says FARO development should only begin after FAR stabilizes, but the repository already contains an active `frameworks/FARO/` tree whose README states that FARO constitutes the operational layer and that the operational framework is under active development, with operation/theory documents present. Without reclassifying or updating those existing FARO artifacts, the FAR README now gives contributors contradictory status guidance about whether FARO work is future-blocked or currently active.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Define candidate generation in the canonical workflow**

This closes the earlier gap by saying candidate generation is explicitly placed in Stage 6, but the commit never updates `frameworks/FAR/workflow.md`, which the FAR docs declare as the canonical source for the stage sequence; its Stage 6 still only describes transformations and contains no candidate-generation rule. A Phase 3 or v1.0 audit that follows the canonical workflow will still see this placement unresolved, so either add the Stage 6/Stage 7 boundary to `workflow.md` or keep the structural audit gap open.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Advance FAR status past the completed Phase 2 gate**

This updated status is now inconsistent with the same commit's audit record, which marks Phase 2 complete and says FAR is ready to proceed to Phase 3 methodology audit; `methodology.md` and `application.md` also still report Phase 1 stabilization. Readers using the FAR entry point will be sent back into a finished phase instead of the remaining methodology/consistency gates, so synchronize these status blocks with the declared Phase 2 completion or do not mark the audit complete.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not mark Phase 3 complete while application is stale**

The audit lists `frameworks/FAR/application.md` as reviewed, but that document was not updated for this Phase 3 policy change: its application requirements still end at recording a resolution and preserving reproducibility (`application.md` lines 37-47), and its status remains Phase 1 (`application.md` line 88). Since this commit changes the canonical workflow/methodology to closure statuses and artifact-based reconstructibility, declaring all Phase 3 corrections implemented here allows Phase 4 to proceed while the synchronization criterion for workflow/methodology/application is still unmet.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require revision records in the canonical workflow**

The new stability criterion says FAR shall require revision records whenever an investigation revisits an earlier stage (`FAR-v1.0-criteria.md` line 67), but the canonical workflow only says those returns “should record” the revision details. For iterative investigations, that makes the record optional at the workflow source, so a missing revision record can still appear compliant despite the required policy and the audit's claim that revision records are required.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep FAR status docs synchronized before passing the audit**

This pass is used to clear the v1.0 gate, but in the repository context I inspected `frameworks/FAR/methodology.md` still says the current work is the Phase 3 methodology audit and preparing for Phase 4, while `frameworks/FAR/application.md` still says the application is under Phase 1 canonical stabilization. With those current-status sections left unchanged, the Phase 4 audit preserves cross-document drift in the exact FAR document set it certifies, so the follow-up freeze milestone can be based on a false completion signal.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep the FARE expansion rule consistent**

This broadens the governance rule to allow new FARE definitions when FAR, FARO, or FARA requires them, but the same status document still says FARE Mathematics v0.1 “shall not expand unless FAR requires mathematical support” in `docs/project-status.md:30`. Once FARO planning starts, a FARO-driven mathematical requirement is simultaneously allowed by this rule and disallowed by the earlier stable-milestone summary, so the milestone governance remains ambiguous unless both statements are updated together.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Update FAR status before freezing it**

This milestone designates `frameworks/FAR/README.md` as Stable, but that file's Current Status still says FAR is only eligible for a stable freeze after review/merge and that FARO should wait until the milestone is recorded (`frameworks/FAR/README.md:19-23`). After this commit the root README and project status say FARO planning has begun, so readers following a newly frozen component get contradictory pre-freeze guidance; update the stale status before marking the file stable.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Add the missing FARE dependency field**

The architecture checklist says every FARO operation shall specify these dependencies, but it skips the `FARE Dependency` field that `operation-interface-standard.md` makes required, including an explicit “none required” statement when applicable. In contexts where an operation has no mathematical dependency, following this architecture document would still leave the operation non-conformant with the interface standard and the FARO v1.0 criteria, weakening the FARE freeze boundary this phase is trying to preserve.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clarify whether execution may determine admissibility**

This exception makes execution operations allowed to determine admissibility when they use a defined FAR reasoning calculus, but the same new document states that “Execution does not determine truth, admissibility, or resolution correctness.” For any automated execution tool that applies a calculus, auditors now have conflicting rules about whether the resulting admissibility classification is a valid FARO execution output, so the allowed/prohibited boundary should be reconciled.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Update FARO README status for Phase 8**

When this status document moves active development to Phase 8, `frameworks/FARO/README.md` still says FARO has entered Phase 7 architecture stabilization and its notes still tell readers to proceed by stabilizing the architecture. Since this commit also declares Phase 7 complete, users who start from the FARO README get the wrong active milestone and may continue Phase 7 work instead of the Phase 8 methodology audit; please update the README status/notes or keep the project status at Phase 7 until they are synchronized.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Rework the failure-mode pass before advancing Phase 8**

This pass result is not supported by the referenced category documents: in `frameworks/FARO/{execution,reporting,operational-evaluation}.md`, there is no category-level failure-mode definition for incomplete, invalid, missing-input, or boundary-related failures; only `auditing.md` actually defines incomplete/invalid audit outcomes. Because FARO v1.0 criteria require the methodology audit to cover failure modes, this lets Phase 8 advance with an unmet audit requirement rather than recording a blocker or adding the missing failure modes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep the audit-record gate in the criteria**

When the stable milestone relies on this Phase 9 finding, it now claims the criteria document records the required audit records, but this same commit replaced the prior `Audit Records Present` criterion with only `Consistency Audit Complete`. That removes the explicit gate that the Phase 6/7/8/9 audit records remain preserved before FARO v1.0 Stable, so a future freeze checklist could pass even if those provenance artifacts are missing or renamed, contrary to the charter's provenance/auditability requirement.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Update canonical FARO status before declaring stability**

This declaration conflicts with unchanged canonical FARO docs: `frameworks/FARO/README.md:13-15` still says FARO is only eligible and not formally v1.0 Stable until the milestone is recorded, and `frameworks/FARO/FARO-v1.0-criteria.md:115` still says FARO is only eligible for the milestone PR. Since the updated reading order sends readers to those canonical documents after this new status, the repository now reports contradictory accepted statuses; update those docs in this commit or defer the stable declaration.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not let unproven FARM drive FARE expansion**

While the Phase 10 audit still has to decide whether FARM should exist and the milestone says FARM must prove responsibilities before canonical expansion, this effective-immediate rule lets any FARM requirement justify new FARE definitions or theorems. In the FARM-scoping context, that bypasses the audit/formalization gate and contradicts `frameworks/FARE/README.md`'s current statement that FARM is not an existing FARE dependency, so FARE Mathematics v0.1 can expand on a candidate layer before the repository has accepted it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Archive the superseded Phase 10 audit record**

By deleting this initiated audit instead of archiving or recording it as superseded, the current tree loses the only in-repository provenance that FARM planning originally opened as Phase 10 with an unresolved necessity verdict; after the diff, a repo-wide search no longer finds that initial verdict text. The root AGENTS.md requires compliance with `docs/governance/research-execution-charter.md`, whose minimality rule says to archive rather than remove unique information, so the renumbering should preserve this historical audit state outside the new completed Phase 1 record.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Add FARM canonical documents to the canonical map**

These new FARM files are now presented as canonical documents, but `docs/CANONICAL_MAP.md` still has no FARM section or entries (I checked the map and repo-wide FARM references). Since the map states it is the canonical-location index for major concepts, leaving these documents only in the FARM README makes the repository's canonical navigation disagree and can route future Phase 3 updates to the wrong or undiscoverable source.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Sync the FARM README before closing Phase 4**

With this update, project status says Phase 3 and Phase 4 are complete, but `frameworks/FARM/README.md` still says the Phase 3 methodology audit is initiated and its next step is to run Phase 3. Since the new Phase 4 audit explicitly includes the FARM README in scope, readers following the FARM entry point get stale guidance and the no-blockers verdict is not reconstructible until the README is updated or the inconsistency is otherwise resolved.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Align the FARM stable component scope**

This adds the Phase 1 through Phase 4 audit records to the FARM stable component set, but the new `docs/milestones/FARM-v1.0-Stable.md` Stable Components section lists only the eight `frameworks/FARM` documents. Because the newly added change policy applies to stable FARM documents, readers now have two conflicting scopes for whether those audit records require formal review; either include the audit records in the milestone or do not mark them stable here.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recheck placeholder search before recording a pass**

The repository already contains matches for this search, so the audit records a false preliminary pass. In the parent tree, `git grep -n -i -E '\b(dummy|temp|placeholder|TODO)\b'` finds live files such as `foundations/discovery/knowledge/evidence/README.md` and several sibling README files saying they are “pilot placeholder” directories; leaving this as “no results” can cause the post-v1 audit to miss required cleanup before worked examples proceed.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reopen the FARE alignment check**

This pass is inaccurate for the post-v1 stack: in this commit, `README.md`'s navigation/reading order lists framework material for FAR/FARA/FARO/FARM but omits FARE, and `docs/CANONICAL_MAP.md` has no FARE section or entries, even though `docs/project-status.md` and this audit classify FARE Mathematics v0.1 as frozen. Since the audit scope includes missing canonical entries, marking alignment as passed lets the worked-example gate proceed while the frozen FARE layer is still absent from the top-level canonical navigation.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore the missing FARE canonical components**

When contributors use this new map as the FARE navigation hub, it drops canonical FARE components that the authoritative FARE spec defines at `frameworks/FARE/specification.md` lines 67-123 (`investigations/`, `theory/`, `proofs/`, and `meta/`). Because this section only links the mathematics/index/definitions rows, those accepted proof and governance materials are no longer discoverable from the canonical map after this normalization; please add the missing FARE components or label the section as intentionally partial.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Align the roadmap version with the active milestone**

This introduces a new `v0.2.0` next-phase roadmap even though the repository already records `docs/releases/project-far-v0.4.md` as the active roadmap milestone and lists the same CI/proposition/lemma/grammar/Lean/proof-step targets there. Under the project charter's single-canonical-location rule, contributors now have two competing roadmap artifacts and the newly added one points them back to an obsolete post-initial-release phase; update or consolidate this plan with the active v0.4 roadmap instead of adding a separate v0.2.0 plan.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include non-theorem nodes in the cycle graph**

When proposition/lemma metadata is validated, dependencies involving those IDs are accepted as known dependencies but never inserted into the graph passed to `validate_no_cycles()` because the graph is initialized only with theorem IDs. In contexts like a theorem depending on `P-001` and `P-001` depending back on that theorem, or two propositions depending on each other, both dependency scripts still pass because those edges are absent from the returned graph, so the new proposition/lemma metadata can become circular without detection.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include P-009 in the generated index**

`theory/metadata/propositions.yaml` adds `P-009` and the proposition catalog contains it, but the committed generated proposition index stops at `P-008`. Anyone using this generated index as the auditable metadata view will miss the proposed Representation Structure Independence proposition, and the current workflow only smoke-runs the generator without checking for a dirty diff, so this stale generated artifact can persist unnoticed.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve ID checks for existing catalogs**

Because this helper is still used for propositions and lemmas, accepting a title match means a metadata entry with a mistyped or stale `P-*`/`L-*` id now passes as long as the source file mentions the title. The new definition/axiom catalogs may need title-based anchoring because their Markdown sources lack `DEF-*` ids, but applying the fallback globally weakens the stable identifier check that protects existing dependency metadata; keep strict id matching for proposition/lemma sources or make the fallback opt-in for the new catalogs.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Add the definition dependency to T-001 metadata**

This proof object now makes `DEF-019` an explicit premise for proving `T-001`, but `theory/metadata/theorems.yaml` still lists only `L-001` through `L-005` as T-001 dependencies. In the dependency/audit checks I inspected, `validate_dependencies()` builds the theorem graph solely from that metadata, so changes to the Minimal definition will not be tracked as affecting this theorem even though the machine-readable proof depends on it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Model the countermodel obligations as inputs**

Here `p2` is only the conditional proof method and `p4` only states L-001's necessity claim; the proof object never establishes the antecedent that a countermodel with the other four primitives exists and fails to express scoped reasoning. Because this same pattern drives s2–s6 after T-002 is added to `REQUIRED_PROOF_OBJECT_THEOREMS`, the required machine-readable proof can be accepted while the central countermodel obligations from `theory/proofs/T-002-primitive-independence.md` remain only in free-text justification rather than in the auditable proof graph.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Prove T exists before conjoining it**

When `R` has no specified transition executions, `s6` only establishes a conditional/permission that `T` may be empty or partial; it does not assert an existing trace component for that case. Conjoining `s6` with `s5` into the unconditional statement `R has C and T` leaves the tuple-existence proof unsupported exactly for the no-specified-trace scenario that T-003 explicitly allows.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use universal generalization for arbitrary R**

This step derives a universal theorem from the construction for an arbitrary `R`, but labels the inference as `universal_instantiation`, which goes in the opposite direction: from a universal statement to a particular instance. Since the available inputs are the local arbitrary assumption and the constructed tuple, consumers of the proof object will see the final conclusion justified by an invalid rule label.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve L-008 in the T-005 proof object**

For T-005, `theory/metadata/theorems.yaml` lists `L-008` as a dependency, and `theory/lemmas/core-lemmas.md` uses that lemma to require source state, target state, rule, and admissibility status before constructing a transition signature. This proof object jumps from `s4` to the final representability claim without citing `L-008` or recording those specified components, so proof-object consumers can validate a T-005 proof for an explicitly specified transition while the required construction premise is absent.
